title: The Base Shift in an Auto Loans Due Day Realignment, by the Borrower's Card Activity
content:
The base shift carried into a realignment of the due day on a loan of the Auto Loans line is read from the borrower's Personal Credit Cards account: the purchases posted to it over the last twelve months, and the count of purchases posted to it in the last three.

| Card purchases over the last twelve months | Card purchases posted in the last three months | Base shift |
|---|---|---|
| At least 9000.00 USD | At least 12 | 8 days |
| At least 3000.00 USD, with either reading short of the row above | At least 4, with either reading short of the row above | 5 days |
| Any other reading | Any other reading | 3 days |

The base shift is 8 days where the borrower's card purchases over the last twelve months total at least 9000.00 USD and at least 12 card purchases have posted in the last three months.

It is 5 days where those purchases total at least 3000.00 USD and at least 4 card purchases have posted in the last three months, while either those purchases fall short of 9000.00 USD or that count falls short of 12.

It is 3 days for every other borrower.

## The two readings are of the same card, over different windows

The first reading sums the amounts of purchases posted over twelve months. The second counts purchases posted over three months. Both are taken from the borrower's account in the Personal Credit Cards line, and the three months of the second reading lie inside the twelve of the first.

## Where a borrower falls between the rows

A borrower with 9000.00 USD of purchases over twelve months but 11 purchases in the last three takes 5 days, both middle-row readings being met while the count falls short of 12.

A borrower with 3 purchases in the last three months takes 3 days whatever their twelve-month total, the count falling short of 4.

A borrower with 20000.00 USD of purchases over twelve months and 12 in the last three takes 8 days.
